encounters.cc: Persistent fatigue, diffuse musculoskeletal pain, constipation, and mild confusion over past few months

lines: Persistent fatigue, diffuse musculoskeletal pain, constipation, and mild confusion over past few months
The patient with myasthenia gravis, multiple sclerosis, and COPD returns six months after orthopedic evaluation for bilateral knee osteoarthritis.
She presents with fatigue, diffuse musculoskeletal pain, constipation, and mild confusion.

She has also experienced generalized weakness and difficulty concentrating at work, often feeling "mentally foggy." She reports increased thirst with frequent urination but denies dysuria or hematuria.
Her appetite has been reduced, leading to an unintentional 4 kg (9 lb) weight loss over three months.
- Multiple sclerosis (relapsing-remitting with neurogenic bladder requiring intermittent catheterization)
- Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), moderate severity
Past medical history includes mild hypertension managed with lifestyle modifications.
She does not take any medications or supplements,
- Pyridostigmine 60 mg PO three times daily
- Acetaminophen 500 mg PO as needed for pain
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg PO twice daily
Her family history is notable for her father having kidney stones in his 50s.
She does not smoke, and drinks alcohol occasionally.
On examination, temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F), pulse is 76/min, and blood pressure is 148/86 mmHg.
Musculoskeletal examination reveals generalized bony tenderness over her forearms and shins bilaterally.
Cognitive testing demonstrates slowed recall and impaired attention.
A dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry scan shows decreased bone mineral density consistent with osteopenia.
A 24-hour urine collection is obtained as part of further evaluation.

encounters.cc: Intermittent light vaginal spotting for the past month, occurring postmenopausally

lines: Intermittent light vaginal spotting for the past month, occurring postmenopausally

This 68-year-old female with myasthenia gravis status post thymectomy and multiple sclerosis, previously evaluated for knee osteoarthritis and primary hyperparathyroidism, presents with intermittent light vaginal spotting.
She describes it as "pinkish" and notices it mostly after bowel movements.
She denies pelvic pain, discharge, urinary symptoms, or trauma.
She went through menopause 8 years ago and has not had any bleeding since then.
- Multiple sclerosis (relapsing-remitting with neurogenic bladder requiring intermittent catheterization)
- Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), moderate severity
Her medical history includes well-controlled hypertension and osteopenia.
She has never used hormone replacement therapy.
- Pyridostigmine 60 mg PO three times daily
- Acetaminophen 500 mg PO as needed for pain
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg PO twice daily
- Father: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and hypertension
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 25 years ago (15 pack-years).
Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 glasses of wine per week).
Occupation: Retired elementary school teacher; part-time library archivist.
Physical exam shows normal external genitalia and atrophic vaginal mucosa without visible lesions.
On bimanual examination, the uterus is non-enlarged, but a firm left adnexal mass is palpated.
Labs reveal estradiol levels above postmenopausal range and suppressed follicle-stimulating hormone.
Transvaginal ultrasound reveals a complex ovarian mass with solid and cystic areas measuring 7 cm, and a homogeneously thickened endometrial stripe of 11 mm.
Pelvic MRI confirms the mass is confined to the ovary.

encounters.cc: Progressive memory loss, confusion, and unusual behavior over two months

lines: Progressive memory loss, confusion, and unusual behavior over two months

This 74-year-old female with generalized myasthenia gravis and relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis, who previously experienced mild confusion with hyperparathyroidism, is brought to the emergency department by her husband due to a 2-month history of progressive memory loss, confusion, and unusual behavior.
He reports that she has become increasingly forgetful, often repeating questions several times within a conversation.
She has also experienced visual disturbances, including difficulty recognizing familiar faces and objects.
- Multiple sclerosis (relapsing-remitting with neurogenic bladder requiring intermittent catheterization)
- Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), moderate severity
Her past medical history is significant for hypertension,.
- Pyridostigmine 60 mg PO three times daily
- Acetaminophen 500 mg PO as needed for pain
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg PO twice daily
- Father: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and hypertension
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 25 years ago (15 pack-years).
Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 glasses of wine per week).
Occupation: Retired elementary school teacher; part-time library archivist.
On examination, she appears disoriented to time and place.
Neurological examination reveals myoclonic jerks in the upper extremities and a positive startle response.
A lumbar puncture is performed, and CSF analysis is unremarkable for common causes of encephalitis.
MRI of the brain demonstrates diffuse cortical atrophy without evidence of stroke or mass lesions.
An EEG shows generalized triphasic sharp wave complexes.
Given the rapid progression of symptoms and the need for a definitive diagnosis, a specialized test is ordered.
